gap: No result ChatGPT got states that AndroidPCTV's reviewer (Kim) measured the QIDI Max4 at 56 dB in normal printing, 62 dB with the Polar Cooler and 65 dB with the QIDI BOX, against 48 dB for the QIDI Plus5. On those two runs, ChatGPT's 'best for maximum size' pick was 8 dB louder than its 'best value' pick.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us 'Large enclosed 3D printers' (cited) and 'Chamber temperature specs' (cited). Both pages say their figures are maker specs only: build volume, maximum chamber temperature, filtration and launch price. Neither gives a noise level, a chamber temperature someone actually reached, a print time or a power draw. Creative Bloq's guide (cited) was cut off when I fetched it, so I could not check whether it has measured figures. None of the top results' titles suggest a side-by-side of measured figures.
decides: This confirms the size-versus-value split and adds a cost the answer never mentions. The Max4's 390 × 390 × 340 mm bed comes with clearly more measured noise than the Plus5: 56 dB against 48 dB, and up to 65 dB when the QIDI BOX is running. The same reviewer timed a PLA Benchy at 18 min on the Max4 and 17 min on the Plus5, so the larger machine is not faster on small parts. Someone printing in a home office who doesn't need more than 320 mm would be better served by the Plus5. For the K2 Plus, Dejan at HowToMechatronics weighed 350 g of purge waste for 83 g of multicolour parts. ChatGPT sold the K2 Plus partly on 'optional multicolor printing', and that figure weakens the point. I found no named measurement for the Bambu H2S or Prusa CORE One L+, so this angle can't change their places.

unsourced: Bambu Lab H2S: I found no noise, chamber-temperature, power or print-time measurement by a named reviewer. The Tom's Hardware review ('The One We Wanted') and TechRadar's H2S review were cut off when I fetched them, Fabbaloo's hands-on returned 403, and search results only repeated Bambu's '<50 dB' rating.

QIDI Max4: AndroidPCTV and the search results reported no measured power draw or chamber temperature reached. Nikktech's Max4 Combo review, which apparently includes power tests, returned 403, and pulling it directly would have needed curl, which needed approval and wasn't run.

Creality K2 Plus: I found no independent noise figure. TechRadar's '45 dB at 300 mm/s' (seen only in a search snippet) matches Creality's own '≤45 dB, Creality Lab' rating and could not be checked because the page was cut off. Tom's Hardware's K2 Plus review was also cut off.

Prusa CORE One L+: I found no measured chamber temperature, noise or print time from a named reviewer. TechRadar's CORE One L review describes the chamber as reaching 'around 60°C' (from a search snippet; I didn't open the page) and gives no test reading.
Rival pages: the Creative Bloq buying guide that ChatGPT cited was cut off after its title, so I could not check whether it includes measured figures.
I did not check US prices; that was outside this measurement angle and the tool budget.
